summary: The 4x M8 pattern matches INT-001 on nominal positions, but the part is 5 mm over the hard envelope (CON-001). Under the general tolerance the bolts are not sure to enter, flush heads on a 10 mm base leave too little seat under the head, and the datums do not line up with the load case or the pin hole function.

flags.title: Part length 125 mm exceeds the 120 mm envelope
flags.evidence: snapshot parts[0].bbox_mm.size = [125, 60, 40]; dimension D2@Base = 125.0 mm. Blueprint CON-001 (hard): envelope <= 120 x 60 x 40 mm. X is 5 mm over; Y and Z are exactly at the limit. The hole pattern sits at x = 20 and 100 (holes[0].centre_mm x = 20, 80 mm pitch), so its centre is x = 60, the midpoint of a 120 mm part. This suggests 120 was intended.
flags.recommendation: Set D2@Base to 120 mm. The hole pattern then sits centred with 20 mm edge distance at both ends. Check that Upright and Pocket1 still fit inside x 0..120 after the change, and re-snapshot the bbox.

flags.title: Bolt pattern position not controlled: worst case leaves no room for the bolt to enter
flags.evidence: Nominally the pattern passes: 4x on an 80 x 40 rectangle (holes[0].pattern, count_same = 4) matches INT-001 and CON-002. Chain: allowed radial mismatch per hole = (clearance hole 8.4 - bolt 8.0)/2 = 0.20 mm, assuming the wall plate is tapped (fixed fastener; INT-001 does not say). The holes carry no tolerance (dimensions[] has no pitch dimension with tolerance; the drawing has no position callout). Assumed ISO 2768-mK (blueprint section 6): 80 +/-0.3 and 40 +/-0.3. Bracket alone, best-fit centred: +/-0.15 in x and +/-0.15 in y, giving radial 0.21 mm > 0.20, so the margin is -0.01 mm. Adding a wall plate also at mK: worst case radial = sqrt(0.30^2 + 0.30^2) = 0.42 mm (margin -0.22). RSS radial approx. 0.30 mm (margin -0.10). Both close below zero. Assumed values: mK tolerances on the pitch, a perfect bolt, a tapped plate.
flags.recommendation: Give the 4 holes a position tolerance relative to datums A|B|C, e.g. position Ø0.3 at MMC for the fixed-fastener case (hole MMC 8.4, so Ø0.4 is available in total). Alternatively, state in INT-001 that the wall plate uses clearance holes with nuts (floating fastener), which doubles the allowance. The hole diameter itself is for Standards.

suggested_change.detail: Add to the 4X Ø8.4 hole callout (RD3) a position tolerance Ø0.3 (M) | A | B | C, and define B and C (see assembly.datums)

flags.title: Flush M8 heads on a 10 mm base leave a seat too thin to take the bolt preload; bolt grade, length and engagement are not defined
flags.evidence: Base thickness D1@Base = 10 mm (PAR-001). ISO 4762 M8 head: k = 8.0 max / 7.64 min, dk = 13. As modelled, counterbore depth 6 gives a 4 mm seat under the head, but the head sticks out 1.54 to 2.1 mm (worst case with cbore 6 +/-0.1 mK), so CON-002 'flush' is not met. The counterbore depth itself is Standards' topic. A flush counterbore of about 8.4 mm leaves a seat of about 1.6 mm. Pull-through check at an assumed 8.8 preload FM approx. 17.5 kN: shear area pi x 13 x 1.6 = 65 mm2, so tau approx. 270 MPa, above the shear strength of 6082-T6 (approx. 190 MPa). The current 4 mm seat gives approx. 107 MPa (passes). Head bearing pressure: 17.5 kN / (pi/4 x (13^2 - 8.4^2) = 77 mm2) = approx. 226 MPa, close to the VDI 2230 limit for AlMgSi1 (approx. 260 MPa). Grade 12.9 (approx. 29 kN) would exceed it. An ISO 7089 M8 washer (OD 16) does not fit the Ø15 counterbore. CON-002 does not give the bolt grade. INT-001 does not give wall plate thickness or material, so bolt length and engagement (>= 1.5d = 12 mm if the plate is tapped aluminium) cannot be checked.
flags.recommendation: Make the material under each head at least approx. 5 mm thick with a flush counterbore of approx. 8.5 mm. Either raise PAR-001 to 14 mm (Z envelope 40 still holds; mass goes up), or add 14 mm thick pads around the 4 holes only. Specify bolt grade 8.8 with tightening torque reduced for aluminium. Add wall plate thickness, material and thread to INT-001 so bolt length = grip + engagement can be chosen.

suggested_change.detail: Option A: set D1@Base (PAR-001) 10 -> 14 mm and the counterbore depth to approx. 8.5 mm. Option B: 14 mm bosses at the 4 hole positions. Also add the bolt grade to CON-002 and the wall plate definition to INT-001.

flags.title: Datum A does not match the load case, and the hole pattern has no secondary or tertiary datum
flags.evidence: INT-001: datum A = back face (-z). The snapshot agrees: the -z face is a single 7500 mm2 face (= 125 x 60, the whole base) and the hole axes are [0,0,1], so the base bolts flat to the wall. The part reaches only 40 mm from datum A (bbox z = 40). Yet REQ-001 and section 7 put the load at 100 mm from the wall, and the bending check uses the base section 60 x 10 (W = 60 x 10^2/6). That only fits a wall at an x-end face. With the base clamped flat to the wall, the load goes through bolt tension and prying and through the upright, not through bending of the base. INT-001 also defines only datum A, so the 80 x 40 pattern has nothing in X or Y to locate from.
flags.recommendation: Confirm which face mounts to the wall and where the 100 mm load acts. If -z is correct, rewrite the section 7 load path (bolt tension with prying: approx. 49 N·m over an 80 or 40 mm row spacing, plus bending at the upright root). Add datum B and datum C to INT-001 (e.g. the -y edge and the -x edge, or hole-to-hole) and put them on the drawing.

suggested_change.detail: INT-001: add datum B and datum C that match how the bracket locates on the wall plate. Section 7: recompute for the base-on-wall load path, or fix the datum A face.

flags.title: Pin hole has no fit and no declared mating part
flags.evidence: holes[1]: Ø3.0, blind, depth 36, axis [1,0,0], centre (0,30,25), so it sits in the upright from the -x face. The dimension D1@Pin hole has tolerance = null, so ISO 2768-m Ø3 +/-0.1 applies. That is too loose to locate or hold a dowel. Blueprint section 5 has no interface for this pin. The drawing has no callout for it (drawings[0].problems).
flags.recommendation: Add an INT-002 saying what the pin does. For a pressed ISO 8734 dowel, use H7 in the hole (dowel m6). For a removable locating pin, use H7/g6. Because the hole is blind, add a vent (a cross-hole or a flat on the pin) or use an extractable dowel with an internal thread, so it can be pressed in and taken out. Fit designation and drill depth belong to Standards and DFM.

suggested_change.detail: Add INT-002 for the Ø3 pin with its function and fit (e.g. Ø3 H7 for an m6 dowel), then tolerance D1@Pin hole to match.

flags.title: Hex key access over the M8 heads could not be checked: upright position unknown
flags.evidence: An M8 ISO 4762 head needs a 6 mm hex key. Clear zone needed above each hole: the Ø15 counterbore column, plus about Ø25 (13 + 2 x 6) for a T-handle or bit socket, i.e. radius 12.5 mm from the hole axis. The holes nearest the -x end are at x = 20, so that zone spans x 7.5..32.5. The pin hole at x = 0, z = 25 shows the upright reaches the -x region above the base, but the snapshot gives no position or thickness for the upright (features[] 'Upright' has no dimensions).
flags.recommendation: Snapshot the Upright dimensions or an iso screenshot. Confirm there is a clear vertical column of at least Ø25 to z = 40 above all 4 holes, or that a straight-in L-key with its short arm fits under any overhang. Fit the bolts before anything is mounted on the upright.

suggested_change.detail: Re-snapshot with the Upright dimensions or an image
